column1: # layout-tiers.tsv — the machine-readable surface-to-tier manifest for the phase-35
# horizontal layout contract. Read by scripts/check-layout-width-contract.sh.
# WHY A MANIFEST AND NOT A PARAGRAPH. The 1400px cap this phase deleted arrived as a
# stock shadcn scaffold block and stayed for the life of the product because nothing was
# watching. A document records what someone intended; this file is what the gate reads,
# so the declared surface set and the enforcement cannot disagree. Plan 35-11 writes the
# prose a person reads; this is the thing that reds a pull request.
# FORMAT. One claim per line. EXACTLY TWO fields, separated by a SINGLE TAB:
#     <repo-relative path><TAB><claim>
# A row that does not split into exactly two non-empty fields is a VOID, not a skip.
# Consecutive tabs collapse under a tab field separator, so an empty field shifts every
# later column and the gate would then be reasoning about the wrong data while reporting
# success. That trap has been paid for in this repository before.
# Blank lines and lines whose first character is `#` are skipped. Reasons therefore live
# in comments ABOVE the rows they explain, never inside a row.
# CLAIM GRAMMAR
#   shell | index | detail | marketing
#       The file DECLARES that tier: its comment-stripped source contains
#       data-width-tier="<tier>". Checked in both directions by G-6.
#   N/A
#       The surface was EXAMINED and DELIBERATELY LEFT UNTIERED. Its comment-stripped
#       source must declare no tier at all. This claim exists because a manifest listing
#       only what IS tiered cannot express "this was considered and left alone" — a later
#       reader sees an absence and reads it as an oversight. An unstated boundary reads as
#       covered.
#   vocabulary
#       The single file allowed to hold the three tier class literals. G-1 reads this row
#       rather than hard-coding the path, so moving the vocabulary is a manifest edit and
#       not a gate edit.
#   parity:<family>:<band-token>
#       The file is a member of a width FAMILY whose members must all render at the same
#       band, and its comment-stripped source must carry <band-token> and no other band
#       token. Used for surfaces that have no tier assignment but must still agree with
#       each other. Checked by G-4.
# A path may appear on more than one row when more than one claim is true of it: the
# /shop/[slug] files are each both N/A (no tier assigned) and a parity member (they must
# nevertheless agree with one another).
# SHELL — the dashboard chrome. One line, inherited by all 21 authenticated routes.
frontend/components/dashboard/dashboard-shell.tsx
# INDEX — resource-index surfaces, fluid to the shell cap. Thirteen surfaces.
# The Index tier applies NO class: "fluid to shell" is the documented pattern for
# data-dense lists (Polaris prescribes a full-width page for lists with many columns,
# Carbon ships a full-width escape from its own grid, Lightspeed's shell is uncapped).
# The tier is nevertheless DECLARED in the DOM, because "uncapped" implemented as an
# absence is a contract no assertion can distinguish from a forgotten cap — ORCH-03
# (orchestrator decision, 2026-08-29, CONTEXT.md section 4b).
# G-7 asserts the absence AT THE DECLARING ELEMENT and deliberately not file-wide.
# Measured on this tree: all five of the original index pages legitimately carry
# max-w-2xl on a modal DialogContent — orders/page.tsx:782,958, products/page.tsx:641,
# customers/page.tsx:419, shops/page.tsx:430. Those are Radix portals rendered outside
# the page container, so the page tier cannot reach them and their width is a modal
# ergonomics decision. A file-scoped no-cap gate would red on correct code.
frontend/app/dashboard/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/orders/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/products/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/customers/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/shops/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/finance/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/marketing/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/kitchen/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/staff/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/onboarding/approvals/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/webhooks/page.tsx
# A [id] DETAIL route deliberately tiered INDEX. Tiered by CONTENT shape, not route
# shape: the reason to open it is a wide, timestamp-heavy delivery log with its own
# horizontal scroll region, and capping it to 1100 would make it scroll MORE than it does
# today. Stated here so the next reader does not "fix" it back to detail. (PATTERNS A-3.)
frontend/app/dashboard/webhooks/[id]/page.tsx
# The flagged-media review queue renders through a component rather than its page.tsx,
# so the declaration lives in components/ — app/dashboard/media/review/page.tsx itself
# carries none, which is why it is recorded below as N/A rather than omitted.
frontend/components/dashboard/media/ReviewQueue.tsx
# DETAIL — ~1100px. Order detail, forms, sequential wizards.
frontend/app/dashboard/orders/[id]/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/products/import/page.tsx
frontend/app/dashboard/onboarding/page.tsx
# MARKETING — ~1280px. Public bands and the chrome rails they must stay equal to.
# The rails are listed alongside the bands on purpose: if a rail and the content beneath
# it declare different tiers, the misalignment this phase removed from the landing page
# reappears inverted. Both directions of G-6 are what keep them together.
frontend/app/page.tsx
frontend/components/marketing/operator-pitch.tsx
frontend/components/marketing/business-model-guide.tsx
frontend/components/marketing/competitive-teardown.tsx
# ORCH-06 (orchestrator decision, 2026-08-29): the outer band of all four /legal/* policy
# routes. The reading measure is held independently at max-w-[68ch] on the columns inside
# it, so widening the band does not widen prose — a tier is a ceiling, not a target.
frontend/components/legal/policy-page.tsx
frontend/components/public/public-header.tsx
frontend/components/public/public-footer.tsx
# ORCH-01 (orchestrator decision, 2026-08-29): public /shop KEEPS the Marketing width and
# does NOT take the Index tier. Flagged owner-visible-if-wrong at the 35-13 gate.
frontend/app/shop/layout.tsx
frontend/app/shop/shop-discovery-client.tsx
frontend/app/shop/loading.tsx
# VOCABULARY — the one file allowed to spell the tier class literals.
frontend/components/layout/content-tier.tsx
# N/A — EXAMINED AND DELIBERATELY LEFT UNTIERED.
# Everything below was inventoried by this phase and left alone with a stated reason.
# None of it is an omission. Each row's reason is in the comment above it.
# THIS ONE CARRIES AN ACTIVE TRAP: DO NOT ADD A CAP HERE. Its <main id="main"> is
# deliberately width-free so children own their bands. Two independent reasons, both
# measured: /shop is a SEPARATE layout tree, and PolicyPage nests inside this one — so a
# cap here would silently narrow surfaces this phase never examined. The concrete
# consequence is recorded at PATTERNS B-12: e2e/unsubscribe-flow.spec.ts asserts no
# horizontal overflow at 375px on /unsubscribe, which is PublicShell + max-w-lg, and is
# "only at risk if PublicShell gains a cap".
frontend/components/public/public-shell.tsx
# The /legal index — a <dl> of company facts plus a linked policy list, held at
# max-w-3xl (768). EXAMINED by ORCH-06 and deliberately left: its content is text with no
# columns to gain from width, and widening a six-item list to 1280 produces a mostly-empty
# band, which is the defect this phase exists to remove reintroduced on a different page.
# Recorded rather than dropped, because an unstated boundary reads as covered.
frontend/app/legal/page.tsx
# The GLOBAL 404 (FE-2, added by the QA-council remediation of 20260902-134741). Held at
# max-w-2xl: it is a signpost with one heading, one line of copy and three links, and a
# wider band would put those links further apart with nothing between them. EXAMINED and
# left untiered for the same ceiling-not-target reason as the surfaces below; the shell
# chrome around it is PublicShell, which carries its own row above.
frontend/app/not-found.tsx
# The /shop/[slug] family. All three are N/A — the surface has not been ASSIGNED a tier
# (PATTERNS A-11 deferred: a tier is a ceiling not a target, 896 is within prose-measure
# territory for a scannable list of dish rows, and the surface is absent from CONTEXT's
# measured baseline). A tier attribute would claim an assignment nobody made. They are
# nevertheless bound to each other by the parity rows further down.
frontend/app/shop/[slug]/loading.tsx
frontend/app/shop/[slug]/shop-detail-client.tsx
frontend/app/shop/[slug]/not-found.tsx
# Storefront and public surfaces that are ALREADY NARROWER than the Detail tier for a
# stated ergonomic reason — a linear checkout step, a receipt, a phone-first history list,
# a two-field lookup form, a single-purpose transactional panel. Each is an instance of
# the ceiling-not-target rule, not an omission.
frontend/app/shop/[slug]/cart/page.tsx
frontend/app/shop/[slug]/checkout/page.tsx
frontend/app/shop/[slug]/orders/[orderNumber]/page.tsx
frontend/app/shop/orders/orders-client.tsx
frontend/app/track/page.tsx
frontend/app/unsubscribe/unsubscribe-content.tsx
# The media review route file is a thin wrapper; its tier is declared by the component it
# renders (listed above under INDEX). Recorded so the page's own empty tier set reads as
# delegation rather than as a gap.
frontend/app/dashboard/media/review/page.tsx
# PARITY FAMILIES — surfaces with no tier assignment that must still agree with one
# another. The failure this catches is measured, not hypothetical.
# Before plan 35-07 the /shop/[slug] skeleton rendered its band at 1280 while the content
# that replaces it renders at 896: the page NARROWED BY 384px the moment real content
# arrived. 35-07 fixed the width and then ran the break arm — reverting the skeleton — and
# recorded that NOTHING on this tree caught it: 14 suites / 146 tests stayed green, and a
# repo-wide search with controls found no test, spec or e2e assertion referencing that
# skeleton at all. It handed the arm to this gate as an explicit debt.
# IT IS A FAMILY OF THREE, NOT A PAIR. A check hard-coded to compare the skeleton and the
# client would leave app/shop/[slug]/not-found.tsx free to drift while reporting the route
# as covered — the same "half a check" failure in the other direction.
frontend/app/shop/[slug]/loading.tsx
frontend/app/shop/[slug]/shop-detail-client.tsx
frontend/app/shop/[slug]/not-found.tsx
